## The problem

Non-major cadets have to learn to reason from data, not just memorize formulas.

## Approach

Six-step statistical investigation method; worked examples on public and synthetic military datasets; interactive apps (CI coverage animation, Wald/Wilson/Agresti-Coull/Clopper-Pearson comparison, z/t/Welch/paired walkthroughs).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Shows the ability to make inference and uncertainty understandable to non-specialist decision makers, a core ORSA briefing skill.
:::

## Results

| Result | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Interactive CI coverage explorer and four-method proportion CI comparison | hypoth_tests/pages/03, conf_int_multiple_methods.py, utils.py (Wilson/AC/CP formulas checked correct) |
| Course guide covers probability through MLR with interactions, ANOVA and Tukey | ma206_course.qmd (identical copy in ma206x and jonday.github.io) |

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- ACFT/ranger_school/plebe datasets are synthetic (labeled in README)
- Third-party CSVs lack source attribution
- Devcontainer points to nonexistent hypoth_tests/z_test.py
- ANOVA and set-notation LaTeX render broken in qmd

## Tools

R, tidyverse, Quarto, Python, Streamlit, scipy, Google Colab
